record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Conditions for existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions
record.original_question: Let p be a prime and F_p the field with p elements. Let (F_p((t)), v_t) be the field of formal Laurent series over F_p with the t-adic valuation. It is shown (Kuhlmann 2001) that there exist henselian defectless valued fields that are not existentially closed in their maximal immediate extensions in the language L_val of valued rings. Specifically, there exists an extension (L, v) of (F_p((t)), v_t) that is a henselian defectless field satisfying the same axiom system, yet (L, v) is not L_val-existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions. A valued field (K, v) is existentially closed in an extension if every existential L_val-sentence true in the extension is already true in (K, v). Is there a natural or 'handy' additional condition on the immediate algebraic extensions of a henselian defectless valued field (K, v) that guarantees (K, v) is existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions?

evidence.quote: Open problem 9: Is there a handy additional condition on the immediate extensions that remedies this situation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L_{\mathrm{val}}$ denote the first-order language of valued rings (the language of rings together with a unary predicate, or equivalently a binary divisibility relation, encoding the valuation). A valued field $(K,v)$ is said to be henselian if its valuation ring satisfies Hensel's lemma. An extension $(L,w)$ of $(K,v)$ is called immediate if the canonical embeddings of value groups $vK \hookrightarrow wL$ and residue fields $Kv \hookrightarrow Lw$ are both isomorphisms. A maximal immediate extension of $(K,v)$ is an immediate extension that admits no proper immediate extension. The defect of a finite extension $(L,w)/(K,v)$ is the integer $d$ such that $[L:K] = d \cdot e \cdot f$, where $e = [wL : vK]$ and $f = [Lw : Kv]$; the field $(K,v)$ is called defectless if every finite extension has defect $1$. Finally, $(K,v)$ is said to be existentially closed in an extension $(L,w)$ (in the language $L_{\mathrm{val}}$) if every existential $L_{\mathrm{val}}$-sentence with parameters from $K$ that holds in $(L,w)$ already holds in $(K,v)$.
        
It is known that there exists a prime $p$ and a henselian defectless extension $(L,v)$ of the formal Laurent series field $(\mathbb{F}_p((t)), v_t)$ such that $(L,v)$ is not $L_{\mathrm{val}}$-existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions, even though $(L,v)$ satisfies the same axiom system (henselian, defectless) as $(\mathbb{F}_p((t)), v_t)$.

Problem. Find a natural additional condition on the immediate algebraic extensions of a henselian defectless valued field $(K,v)$ which, when imposed, guarantees that $(K,v)$ is $L_{\mathrm{val}}$-existentially closed in every maximal immediate extension of $(K,v)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question concerning a sufficient additional condition on immediate algebraic extensions ensuring existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions. No published resolution was identified; the problem appears to remain open.
